highlights.title: Meta’s $25 billion legal loss just put blood in the water
highlights.summary: When attorneys general from across the US announced a $17 billion settlement with Meta this summer, the sum was unprecedented. But a ruling last week by a New Mexico judge blew that number out of the water.
body: The answer depends on a mix of factors, including whether the $25 billion order stands up to Meta’s legal challenges. Meta’s chief legal officer C.J. Mahoney said in a statement that the company is “confident we will prevail on appeal” and called New Mexico’s lawsuit an attempt to impose “a tax on speech.” If the fine sticks, however, it could create a new appetite for Big Tech’s opponents to stick it out in court — or ask for bigger payouts to settle.

“For the settling AGs, they’re going to look at this and maybe experience some regret for all the claims that they waived, and start looking around and trying to figure out what’s left that they didn’t waive, if they can try to get some money like this too,” says Daphne Keller, director of platform regulation at the Stanford Program in Law, Science & Technology. For the many individuals, school districts, and tribes with outstanding claims, “this is very encouraging and will make them hopeful that continuing to litigate aggressively will lead to a big payout,” Keller says.

highlights.title: Wolff rejects Marko's doubts over Russell's future F1 title hopes
highlights.summary: Mercedes chief Toto Wolff has rejected Helmut Marko's suggestion that George Russell has little chance of becoming Formula 1 world champion in the future after being outperformed by his team-mate Kimi Antonelli this season.
body: Antonelli won the United States Grand Prix on Sunday to move to the brink of being crowed the sport's youngest ever champion, with the 20-year-old only needing to finish ninth this weekend in the Mexico City Grand Prix to seal the title with four rounds to spare.

Perhaps the most shocking element of the Italian's historic campaign has been the way he has outperformed Russell, who had begun the season as the clear title favourite after dominating Antonelli during the latter's rookie season last year.

Speaking ahead of Sunday's race in Austin, former Red Bull motorsport advisor Marko told Sky Germany: "Mentally, it's certainly a massive setback and it's a blow. Russell is no longer the number one driver."

"Antonelli has quite clearly taken that spot from him. But Russell is one of the top drivers. I doubt whether he'll ever have another chance at the world title or be given number one status anywhere."

highlights.title: Anthropic’s elaborate plan to keep Wall Street at bay
highlights.summary: Anthropic wants to have it both ways. With its impending IPO, it wants to tap the vast riches of the public markets and insists it doesn't want to compromise its core mission of developing AI safely and for the benefit of humanity.
body: Anthropic’s planned IPO raises questions over whether it can maintain its safe and responsible AI priorities.

Sam Altman, the CEO of Anthropic’s archrival, OpenAI, has cited investor pressures as one reason the company is not pursuing an IPO this year. Anthropic hopes it can resist investor pressures with a mind-boggling governance structure.

University of Pennsylvania law professor Elizabeth Pollman told The Verge that Anthropic has proposed going public with a “unique and complicated governance structure that has not been used before” and that has been “creatively designed for this founder-led and mission-driven company.” Experts say it should give Anthropic freedom to pursue profits without letting shareholders force it to cut corners on safety or rush systems out before they’re adequately tested. But even the strongest legal protections can only go so far, and no corporate structure, no matter how well designed, can completely insulate a public company from the demands of the market.

highlights.title: "This is a serious incident" - Kingdom Come: Deliverance developer Warhorse suffers cyberattack
highlights.summary: Kingdom Come: Deliverance developer Warhorse Studios has confirmed it's suffered a "serious" cyberattack, saying it is currently working to determine the "full extent" of its impact.
body: "To our players and friends," a statement by the studio read. "We're sorry to share that Warhorse Studios has been hit by a cyberattack. We're working with cybersecurity specialists to secure our systems and understand the full extent of what happened. Thank you for standing with us." The message was released at 11am GMT and there hasn't been an update from the studio since. We've separately asked the studio if there have been any developments.

Warhorse CEO Martin Frývaldský discussed the incident in a Czech report (translated by DeepL), saying, "This is a serious incident for Warhorse Studios and for everyone affected. Our immediate priority is to secure our systems, determine the full extent of the breach, and take all necessary steps to protect our employees, partners, and our community. We are devoting all necessary resources and capabilities to resolving this situation."

highlights.title: ’40 Watts From Nowhere’: How a Feisty Pirate Radio Station Stormed the Airwaves in 1990s Silver Lake With Help From the Red Hot Chili Peppers and More
highlights.summary: The 1990s were a very different time — especially in Silver Lake, California — once a fertile neighborhood of artists and musicians and now a pricey hot spot. Three decades ago, the indie music scene was flourishing with homegrown acts like Beck and Rilo Kiley, based around clubs like Spaceland and…
body: The mystique of the scrappy station is told in the new documentary “ 40 Watts From Nowhere,” a fond look back at the Silver Lake music scene and the bands and personalities that came through KBLT. The doc premiered at Slamdance in February and, thanks to Jack Black stepping in as executive producer, it got the attention of Amazon Prime, where begins streaming Tuesday.

KBLT was the brainchild of Sue Carpenter, a journalist and music lover who learned about a “legal bubble” that enabled people to start low-power radio stations without prohibitively expensive FCC licenses. Carpenter learned how to put such a station together from Berkeley, California pirate radio guru Stephen Dunifer, got help building a transmitter, and started her first radio project, KPBJ, in her San Francisco apartment. After moving to L.A., Carpenter (using a pseudonym) selected another food-themed acronym and started making connections to line up DJs.

highlights.title: ‘I was so sick’: is running a marathon while on a GLP-1 a bad idea?
highlights.summary: As the weight-loss drugs become more common, some runners find the side-effects challenging. Here’s what experts say. Women: was your autoimmune condition misdiagnosed? Keri M, a marathoner in her 50s, knew the race would be terrible. This feeling couldn’t be chalked up to inexperience.
body: She ran the 2024 Philadelphia marathon fast enough to earn a coveted spot in this year’s Bank of America Chicago race, one of the eight world marathon majors.

But this half marathon felt different. It was the first time she had raced on a GLP-1. Less than a week beforehand, she had taken her first 2.5mg standard starting dose of tirzepatide, commonly sold under the names Mounjaro and Zepbound, for weight loss.
Throughout the race, Keri felt nauseous, struggling to keep down the energy gels many endurance runners rely on for fuel.
“After that half marathon, I was so sick,” she said. Keri had a “severe” reaction to the 2.5mg dose and, in hindsight, wishes that she had started at a lower dose.

highlights.title: Firefox’s Smart Window adds AI form filling and webpage monitoring
highlights.summary: Mozilla is updating Smart Window - Firefox's AI-powered browsing experience - with a new feature that can help you fill out online forms based on your open tabs. As an example, Mozilla says Smart Window can pull information from your online portfolio or LinkedIn page to paste your work history into…
body: An update to Firefox’s AI browsing experience can draw from your open tabs to help you fill out forms.

You can try out this feature by clicking into a form with at least four text fields. From there, you’ll see an option to “Fill from sources,” which will show all of the tabs Firefox will draw from. You can then select or deselect tabs that you want Firefox to use, and the browser will generate suggestions based on the information in them. This feature currently supports text fields on web forms, but Mozilla is working to add support for dropdown menus and PDFs. Mozilla notes that data from your source pages is shared with Google’s Gemini 3.1 Flash Lite, the AI model that generates the text suggestions.

Along with this update, you can now ask Firefox’s Smart Window to watch a certain webpage for sales, new job listings, and other updates. You can set up a task by typing “/watch” in the Smart Window chat, describing what you’re looking for, and adding the webpages you want to watch. Firefox can then check for updates on a daily or weekly basis, but only when the browser is open.

highlights.summary: Kingdom Come: Deliverance developer Warhorse Studios appears to be the latest game studio hit by a cyberattack. The studio confirmed in a statement that it was affected by a cybersecurity incident and is currently assessing the extent of the damage.
body: “This is a serious incident for Warhorse Studios and everyone affected,” said Martin Frývaldský, CEO of Warhorse Studios. “Our immediate priority is to secure our systems, establish the full extent of the breach, and take the necessary steps to protect our employees, partners, and community. We are dedicating the resources needed to address this situation and will communicate further information as soon as we responsibly can.”
Warhorse said it won’t be conducting interviews or providing additional comments about the situation, and that it will share further verified information when it becomes available.

Video game studios have faced a wave of cyberattacks in recent years, with Grand Theft Auto 6 developer Rockstar Games arguably taking the brunt of it. In September, Rockstar was hacked by the group ShinyHunters. Before that, Cyberleeks hit the company and released stolen GTA 6 gameplay footage and, years prior, Rockstar suffered a major breach which revealed an early development build.

highlights.title: Russell Brand told police he never had non-consensual sex
highlights.summary: His trial hears statements he gave to police between 2023 and 2025, denying allegations against him.
body: Russell Brand told police in interviews in response to allegations of rape and sexual assault that he had never engaged in "non-consensual sexual activity", a court has heard.
Brand, 51, was interviewed four times between 2023 and 2025 by officers.
The TV and media personality is currently on trial at Southwark Crown Court in London on three counts of rape and other offences. He denies all the charges.

Jurors heard on Tuesday that he gave a prepared statement in each of the police interviews. In November 2023, he said: "I have repeatedly stated publicly and written extensively that I led a very promiscuous life, that I have spent years openly denouncing. I have never engaged in non-consensual activity."

highlights.title: A 28-Year-Old DOGE Operative Gutted USAID. HR Had No Record of Him Working There
highlights.summary: Despite the agency's human resources department saying he hadn’t even been onboarded, Jeremy Lewin oversaw the destruction of USAID. It’s not clear he had the legal authority to do so.
body: On March 18, 2025, Secretary of State Marco Rubio handed the reins of the US Agency for International Development to Jeremy Lewin, a 28-year-old graduate of Harvard Law School, former investment banker, and affiliate of Elon Musk’s so-called Department of Government Efficiency. At the time, Lewin’s appointment drew criticism because of his lack of experience in government, diplomacy, or foreign assistance. But for career staff inside the agency, the issues surrounding Lewin’s new role were much more alarming than his thin résumé.

For at least two months, USAID senior staff had no knowledge of how Lewin, who appeared at the agency one day as a policymaker on an obscure detail from the General Services Administration, could have suddenly begun wielding the powers of the agency’s top official.

highlights.title: Genie 4: A new generation of world simulation
highlights.summary: Today, we are announcing Genie 4, our new world model, which unlocks unprecedented realism and improves real-time interactive simulation. Genie 4 is natively multimodal, enabling audio-like music, ambient noises, and interactive dialogue to be simultaneously generated with the world.
body: The Genie 4 model incorporates and builds on capabilities from the Gemini family: Gemini Omni anchors the simulations in real-world appearance and behavior, while other Gemini models provide the complex reasoning needed to help maintain a simulation’s coherence and continuity.
With this foundation, you can set an event in motion, and Genie 4 simulates what happens next: how the world responds, how it sounds, and how the people in it move, react, and speak.

Understanding and simulating the world is a crucial aspect of building AGI. Genie 4 advances our ability to create safe, infinitely variable simulations that can help with everything from developing training environments for robots and agents to unlocking the creation of new interactive experiences.
The following are recordings of real-time interactions from Genie 4, where users use standard keyboard controls for navigation and camera control, and text prompts to steer the scene as it evolves.

highlights.title: Osaka's outfit dazzles again in Japan win as Williams loses to teenager
highlights.summary: Home favourite Naomi Osaka said she wanted to bring "a bit of a show" to the Pan Pacific Open after wearing a Japan-inspired outfit before beating Italy's Jasmine Paolini in the opening round.
body: The seventh seed defeat Paolini in 6-3 7-6 (4) in a match lasting one hour and 37 minutes in Tokyo, saving saved three consecutive set points in the second set before sealing victory in the tiebreak to advance to the second round.

Osaka returned to Tokyo for the first time in four years and wore a blue-and-white, crane-embroidered kimono-inspired outfit designed by Hana Yagi - who created her Wimbledon outfit - as she entered the WTA 500 event.

"I was just really glad that she [Yagi] wanted to work with me again," Osaka said. "I feel like for me I haven't been here in a little bit of a while, so It's just nice to bring a bit of a show here too."

Victory for Osaka avenges her loss to Paolini last year in the Miami Open, their only previous meeting, with the 29-year-old racking up seven aces to her opponent's one during the tournament-opening victory.

highlights.title: Why do we measure root ginger in ‘thumbs’ and centimetres rather than weight? | Kitchen aide
highlights.summary: When it comes to ginger, personal taste often trumps strict precision, say our experts as they get to the root of the issue. Why do so many recipes state the amount of fresh ginger in “thumbs” or centimetres. With it being so variable in shape, why don’t you use weight?
body: Cloake’s fellow columnist Georgina Hayden agrees: “Unlike measuring a ratio of risotto rice to stock, or making a cake, the typical recipes I use ginger in, such as curries, don’t have to be precise,” she says. “After all, cooking should be as instinctive as possible, rather than relying on digital scales.” However, Nick is right in that ginger does vary hugely in shape, Cloake says: “If it was a very thick piece, or it wasn’t thumb-shaped, I’d cut it so the cumulative flesh of the ginger was roughly the same as the cumulative flesh of a thumb. You’re just trying to give a rough amount, without being too prescriptive. But he’s right, we should probably move to grams.”

After all, that’s a big part of cooking, right? When Hayden writes a recipe, she says, its purpose is also to empower home cooks to take a bit of creative licence: “A knob of butter, a pinch of salt, a bunch of herbs … sometimes, vague measurements are a good thing. Also, it’s mad to get out the scales for something as small as ginger.”

body: It’s typical: You wait a decade for a cheap electric truck, and then two come along almost at once. And they’re two radically different products from two radically different automakers that I think will reveal a few preferences from the EV-buying public. One is the Blank Slate, from a brand new startup offering a bare-bones two-door that capitalizes on features the Internet says it wants, like no onboard modem, no touchscreens, and no infotainment system.

The other is the result of one of Detroit’s big three taking a long, hard look at Chinese EVs and asking itself, “How do we make a car that cheap?” Although the Ford Fathom will cost $5,000 more than a Slate, that money does buy an extra pair of doors, modern conveniences like an infotainment system, CarPlay, electric windows, and a vast dealership network to service the car. That may be helpful given how many recalls Ford issues each year.

highlights.title: DeepMind unveils Genie 4 world model promising more realistic physics and humans
highlights.summary: Last year, Google DeepMind sent gaming stocks tumbling with the reveal of its Genie 3 world model. Since then, world models have become a major focus of AI labs around the world, but Google isn't resting on its laurels.
body: It's easy to look at the output of Genie 4 and see a video game, which is why Genie 3 caused so much consternation in the gaming industry. DeepMind doesn't think about it that way, though. According to Google, world models are a key element in the march toward artificial general intelligence (AGI). A world model creates a virtual world, but it doesn't require pre-rendering environments or programming interactive elements. You simply tell the model what you want, and it generates the experience frame by frame in real time as you explore it.

DeepMind says this technology could create infinite training environments for physical robots or unlock new avenues of rapid prototyping for creative fields. Of course, that requires the model to accurately simulate what you want. Genie 4 has several improvements that make its simulations more useful, and that's thanks in part to Google's updated Gemini models.

highlights.title: Industrial Intelligence: The next growth opportunity for manufacturing
highlights.summary: Every manufacturer has its own industrial intelligence. Some is documented, and some resides in the knowledge of experienced workers. Consider an experienced operator preparing to restart a line after a changeover.
body: That combination is industrial intelligence: a manufacturer’s accumulated know-how, operating practices, production data, and understanding of its own business.

The opportunity now is to make more of that intelligence available wherever decisions are made, then connect it to the physical world of manufacturing. The strategic destination is not more agents, but rather to turn the existing business intelligence into an engine for profitable growth.

Expertise has limited reach when it stays with one person, inside one system, or within one plant. Leaders now must determine how to extend that reach without stripping away the context that makes the knowledge useful.

For example, an engineer evaluating a process change needs more than a production record. They need to understand the circumstances behind it: the equipment configuration, the quality requirements, and the trade-offs an operator made. Connecting those elements can help people apply experience beyond the place where it originated.

highlights.summary: Apparently, I’m the person who turns up soaking wet, sucking Haribos. Who needs lifelong friends who know you inside-out when acquaintances tell it like it is? The worst kind of professional relationship is with the person you see twice a year, in a variety of different locations, because whatever…
body: “You were really wet last time!” the photographer exclaimed, remembering our previous meeting back in March. “Well, it’s a wet country,” I replied, before the person we were there to shoot chipped in: “It’s actually in unprecedented drought, but fine.” Then the photographer asked, “Have you thought about getting some wet-weather clothes, if you’re going to cycle?” and I said, “Obviously this is the first time that’s occurred to me, otherwise it would have happened at some point between March and now,” except she didn’t hear me because I had my mouth full of Haribo chewy sours.

“You ate all the Haribos last time,” my colleague observed, and I’ll skip the denials because even though I can’t remember that, it sounds true. Something about getting soaked on a bike makes me powerfully hungry – I think the sense of grievance messes with my blood sugar. “Have you ever thought of having breakfast?” came the next bolt of blue-sky thinking. It’s a great ice-breaker, making such a fist of your life choices that you become a human suggestions box, everyone mucking in with some basic improvements. But this, I insist, was two freak days of 2026; all the others have panned out fine.

highlights.title: From cheap tool to premium subscription: When a beloved app's price skyrockets
highlights.summary: How much are you willing to pay to keep using your favorite app? Maybe you’ve used it for years. Perhaps it performs a function so essential and specific that you couldn’t imagine what you’d do without it.
body: Earlier this year, Evernote, a note-taking app, changed its subscription tiers, forcing some users to go from paying $130 per year to $250. The highest tier now costs more than 3.3 times as much as the most advanced tier did in 2023 and 10 times more than what Evernote charged for annual subscriptions from its 2008 launch until 2016.

That’s just one example of many longstanding consumer pieces of software that have seen dramatic price hikes in recent years. A lifetime pass to Plex, for example, was $75 in 2012. Today, it’s $250. Individual plans for Quicken, Robokiller, and Inkdrop have each doubled in price.

It’s easy to assume that the developers are miscalculating the value of their app or the loyalty of their users. But an unconventionally honest assessment regarding price hikes from Evernote owner Bending Spoons illustrates how owners of legacy software can apply pressure to loyal customers to extract additional revenue.

When Bending Spoons bought Evernote in 2023, the app had a sizable customer base. In a June SEC filing, Bending Spoons explained that it was attracted to Evernote’s 200 million accounts and high user engagement.
points: How much are you willing to pay to keep using your favorite app?

body: Every morning, Michelle Seo receives a briefing from Chattiana, her Muse artificial intelligence agent.

Seo is far from the first person to consume her news with an AI assist. In fact, the trend has become so common that some news outlets are starting to produce content that treats AI agents—not human readers—as the intended audience. This can look like anything from feeds optimized for AI to pieces structured to allow agents to create personalized articles.

“We believe that the media ecosystem is changing,” says Axios chief revenue officer Jacquelyn Cameron. “We see this with open web deteriorating. We see that search is shrinking. We see that hyperpersonalization is surging, that LLMs are becoming more important in the way that people are consuming” their news.

highlights.title: I struggled to come to terms with my mum’s death. Then I swam in the sea and suddenly felt connected to her
highlights.summary: My mother was a keen swimmer, and she lived with depression. I wonder if she found the same respite in the water that has helped heal me since she passed away. It was early morning in late September, off the coast of Kaş in Turkey.
body: Head in the water, the knotted feeling in my throat began to loosen. Breathing came properly. There was respite.

My swimming is far from sophisticated – my strokes are messy and I am mostly kicking from the knees. Still, I manage to move forward, albeit slowly, hugging the coastline of Turkey’s Lycian Way, turning a corner and entering an area of calm. The water is blue-green. Fish glide purposefully beneath, and I’m uplifted when I see a turtle navigating around a rock on the seabed.

I came to Turkey with SwimTrek, a Brighton-based company offering guided open-water swim tours. The plan is to complete 25km over five days. On the one hand, it is a holiday; but for me, the combination of swimming and the sea has become something more than that.

I had been feeling lost as I tried to come to terms with my mum not being here any more, and generally anxious, made worse by sleepless nights. Even on calm days, at times it felt difficult to breathe, the tightness in the throat unrelenting.
points: My mother was a keen swimmer, and she lived with depression.
I wonder if she found the same respite in the water that has helped heal me since she passed away.
